title: Recognition and Cleavage of Human tRNA Methyltransferase TRMT1 by the SARS-CoV-2 Main Protease
authors: D'Oliviera A; Dai X; Mottaghinia S; Olson S; Geissler EP; Etienne L; Zhang Y; Mugridge JS
one_liner_zh: 该文研究SARS-CoV-2蛋白酶对宿主tRNA甲基转移酶TRMT1的识别与切割，涉及蛋白-蛋白互作而非蛋白-DNA互作，虽含分子动力学模拟但对象与课题核心不符。
abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro, or Nsp5) is critical for the production of functional viral proteins during infection and, like many viral proteases, can also target host proteins to subvert their cellular functions. Here, we show that the human tRNA methyltransferase TRMT1 can be recognized and cleaved by SARS-CoV-2 Mpro. TRMT1 installs the N2,N2-dimethylguanosine (m2,2G) modification on mammalian tRNAs, which promotes global protein synthesis and cellular redox homeostasis. We find that Mpro can cleave endogenous TRMT1 in human cell lysate, resulting in removal of the TRMT1 zinc finger domain. TRMT1 proteolysis results in elimination of TRMT1 tRNA methyltransferase activity and reduced tRNA binding affinity. Evolutionary analysis shows that the TRMT1 cleavage site is highly conserved in mammals, except in Muroidea, where TRMT1 is likely resistant to cleavage. In primates, regions outside the cleavage site with rapid evolution could indicate adaptation to ancient viral pathogens. Furthermore, we determined the structure of a TRMT1 peptide in complex with Mpro, revealing a substrate binding conformation distinct from the majority of available Mpro-peptide complexes. Kinetic parameters for peptide cleavage show that the TRMT1(526-536) sequence is cleaved with comparable efficiency to the Mpro-targeted nsp8/9 viral cleavage site. Mutagenesis studies and molecular dynamics simulations together indicate that kinetic discrimination occurs during a later step of Mpro-mediated proteolysis that follows substrate binding. Our results provide new information about the structural basis for Mpro substrate recognition and cleavage, the functional roles of the TRMT1 zinc finger domain in tRNA binding and modification, and the regulation of TRMT1 activity by SARS-CoV-2 Mpro. These studies could inform future therapeutic design targeting Mpro and raise the possibility that proteolysis of human TRMT1 during SARS-CoV-2 infection suppresses protein translation and oxidative stress response to impact viral pathogenesis.
abstract_zh: SARS-CoV-2 主蛋白酶（Mpro，或 Nsp5）在感染期间对功能性病毒蛋白的产生至关重要，并且与许多病毒蛋白酶一样，也能靶向宿主蛋白以颠覆其细胞功能。在此，我们表明人 tRNA 甲基转移酶 TRMT1 可被 SARS-CoV-2 Mpro 识别并切割。TRMT1 在哺乳动物 tRNA 上安装 N2,N2-二甲基鸟苷（m2,2G）修饰，这促进整体蛋白质合成和细胞氧化还原稳态。我们发现 Mpro 能在人细胞裂解液中切割内源性 TRMT1，导致 TRMT1 锌指结构域被移除。TRMT1 的蛋白水解导致其 tRNA 甲基转移酶活性丧失，并降低 tRNA 结合亲和力。进化分析显示，TRMT1 切割位点在哺乳动物中高度保守，但在鼠科（Muroidea）中除外，其中 TRMT1 可能对切割具有抗性。在灵长类动物中，切割位点之外的区域快速进化可能表明对古代病毒病原体的适应。此外，我们解析了 TRMT1 肽与 Mpro 复合物的结构，揭示了一种与大多数现有 Mpro-肽复合物不同的底物结合构象。肽切割的动力学参数显示，TRMT1(526-536) 序列的切割效率与 Mpro 靶向的 nsp8/9 病毒切割位点相当。诱变研究和分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟共同表明，动力学区分发生在底物结合之后的 Mpro 介导蛋白水解的后期步骤。我们的结果提供了关于 Mpro 底物识别和切割的结构基础、TRMT1 锌指结构域在 tRNA 结合和修饰中的功能作用，以及 SARS-CoV-2 Mpro 对 TRMT1 活性调控的新信息。这些研究可为未来靶向 Mpro 的治疗设计提供参考，并提出 SARS-CoV-2 感染期间人 TRMT1 的蛋白水解可能抑制蛋白质翻译和氧化应激反应，从而影响病毒发病机制的的可能性。
